boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Elkin's Ferry (Okolona) record (April 3-4, 1864) in the Camden Expedition [April 1864]. The frozen record also carries the name Okolona. The April 2 rear-guard fight near Okolona and Terre Noir Creek and the April 4 picket fight at Okolona are recorded separately and not added to the ferry fight; the march from Little Rock (from March 23) and Thayer's junction on April 9 are context. Campaign-wide marches, returns, foraging and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads 3rd Division, VII Corps and 2 cavalry brigades [US] and 3 cavalry brigades [CS]; the live field reads zero. Price says Steele's column was estimated at 10,000 men of all arms with 25 guns and 400 wagons, and that only some 1,200 Confederates were actually engaged on April 4. Britton says Steele expected about twelve thousand once Thayer joined, and Price's district held three divisions of about twelve thousand; he names Marmaduke's force as Greene's and Cabell's brigades with four guns, and the Union front line as six companies under Drake. Shelby attacked the rear guard on April 2 with fifteen hundred men.
claims.rationale: Army-level estimates, an engaged figure from the interested side, and unit identifications that differ from the frozen three brigades; the April 2 figure belongs to a separate action. None is adopted as a matched opening strength. The live zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: NPS says Union forces sought the ford because other roads were impassable. Britton says Carr found the river fordable on April 2, Marmaduke bivouacked on the edge of the Little Missouri bottom, the Union guns fell back across Howard's Creek, and Marmaduke then threw up log-and-earth defences about four miles south. A later rise of about three feet covered the lower bottoms.
claims.rationale: Ground and water described by a summary and a history; no map or gauge record. The river's state changed during the operation.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 92 total (US 38; CS 54); the live field reads 55 (US 26; CS 29). Price claims one stand of colors and small arms taken and says Rice was slightly wounded. Britton gives Rice's loss on April 2 as eight killed and thirty-two wounded, Krez's on April 4 at Okolona as three killed and three wounded, and sixteen Confederates captured on April 3; Price says Shelby killed near 100 and captured 60 (read 'GO') on April 2. No inspected passage gives a total for the ferry fight.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. The April 2 and Okolona figures belong to separate actions and are not added.

open_questions: Steele's reports (No. 2), Salomon's, Rice's, McLean's, Norris's, Kittredge's, Drake's and Peetz's reports (Nos. 5-6, 13-16, 18), Engelmann's and Krez's Okolona reports (Nos. 19, 22), Marmaduke's, Greene's and Shelby's reports (Nos. 71-73) and the No. 1 strength table remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Wiley Britton's The Civil War on the Border, volume II (Putnam's, 1899) is a retrospective history described on its title page as based upon official reports and the author's observations; it gives figures from Union and Confederate reports and incomplete Confederate returns, so it is not independent of the Official Records families. Price's report dated Camden, May 1864 is one family of interested Confederate accounts. Official Records Series I, Volume XXXIV, Part 1 is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
